title: Sentin-Harden rule
description: A single audit item with its assessment and commands. The record has two parts of different origin: 'benchmark' is transcribed from the CIS document and limited to identification, everything else is original work. Text fields are bilingual (pl, en) and both are required, so a missing translation cannot pass unnoticed. Commands, categories and impact areas are language neutral and are never translated.

id.description: Our stable rule identifier. It does not change when the benchmark renumbers its items.

benchmark.description: IDENTIFICATION - the only part transcribed from the CIS document, limited to what lets a reader find the item in their own copy of the benchmark.

item.description: Item number in the benchmark. The value TBD means the number has not been confirmed against the document - we do not guess it.

title.description: Short label that allows the item to be located. Do not transcribe the description or rationale.

section.description: Benchmark area, e.g. 'Account Policies > Password Policy'. Lets the pack be matched against the document before item numbers are confirmed.

applies_to_roles.description: Server roles the rule applies to. Absent = applies regardless of role.

risk_category.description: OWN ASSESSMENT. What the attacker gains while the item stays unmet. Never derive it from the L1/L2 level.

disruption.description: OWN ASSESSMENT. Decides whether the change may be applied in bulk.

assessment_state.description: Separates 'checked, no impact' from 'not assessed yet'. An empty impact list must never pose as safety.

description.description: What it defends against and what stops being possible after the change. Original work.

disruption_description.description: Why this disruption class was assigned. Required for anything other than 'none'.

impact_areas.description: Identifiers from impact-areas.yaml. They drive the reverse view and the pre-execution summary. Never translated.

what_breaks.description: Concrete scenarios, not general warnings. The minimum length is deliberately high: a platitude fits in a few words, a described scenario does not.

do_not_apply_when.description: Roles and configurations where this change is a mistake.

audit.description: Read-only stage. The test command MUST NOT change system configuration.

test_command.description: Read-only check. Two output tokens are reserved and must not be matched by 'expected': CHECK_ERROR means the check could not be performed (missing privileges, unavailable subsystem) and maps to the ERROR result; NOT_APPLICABLE means the element does not exist in this edition. Suppressing errors so that a failed check looks like a pass is the worst possible defect in a rule - always separate 'not set' from 'could not read'.

remediation.description: State changing commands. The {{backup_file}} placeholder is filled by the engine with the same path in the backup command and in the rollback command, so rollback knows what to restore.

backup_command.description: Protects the modified resource BEFORE the change, with a scope matching the change exactly.

rollback_command.description: Restores the state from before the change, usually from {{backup_file}}.

runnable.description: Whether the 'Run' button may be shown. The 'Copy' button is always available regardless of this value.

sources.description: Links to the system vendor documentation. Never to CIS content.

allOf.$comment: Hard rule: no backup and rollback means no Run button.
An unassessed rule must never reach bulk mode.
If the impact is described, it must be described concretely, not declaratively.
Disruptive classes require a justification of the assigned class.

text.description: Bilingual text field. Both versions required.
